Subject: Post-demo: performance gating & reservation validation plan

Asha — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same scope for the validation work we discussed.

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary goal: confirm predictable token throughput and 99th/99.9th percentile latency under MedTech’s mixed inference footprint (short clinical prompts + long context batches).
- Decision hinge: whether a Redwood Dedicated reservation (guaranteed capacity + SLA) materially reduces tail latency/cost risk vs running on hyperscaler reserved VMs or on-demand burst.
- Success criteria you mentioned: 95% of requests <= 120ms p50, 99% <= 400ms for short prompts; stable KV-cache hit improvements for repeated user sessions.

What we propose (three validation experiments):
1) Baseline throughput ramp (hyperscaler reserved A100/H100 equivalent vs Redwood Dedicated pool) — repeated ramps from 0 -> target concurrency to measure cold-starts and prefix cache warmup.
2) Tail-latency stress (mixed short/long traffic, 90/10 split) with controlled background noise to simulate other tenant load; verify 99/99.9 tails and modeling of fallback behavior.
3) Failure/recovery simulation — graceful degradation test: drop 30% of nodes in the cluster and measure fallback to compatible variants and request routing latency impact.

What Redwood will provide:
- Test matrix (attached: capacity_validation_matrix.xlsx) with test scripts and sample payloads.
- A load harness (we'll provide k6 scripts + a rust/python client wrapper) and a short checklist to instrument tracing.
- Recommended config set (quantization profiles, batching window, cache retention) for parity across runs.

Open asks for MedTech:
- Confirm the hardware you want us to compare against (A100 vs H100 vs CloudScale X1) — Asha, you mentioned both A100 reserved and an H100 pilot.
- Preferred 2-week window for testing (we propose Oct 18–29).
- Primary test owner/contact and whether you want Redwood to run tests in your cloud account or through Redwood-hosted Dedicated instances.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You confirm hardware/setups and the test window this week.
- We schedule a 30-minute pre-run kickoff to align on instrumentation and access (we'll book after your confirmation).
- Redwood to send SOW draft and test scripts (attached).

Thanks — I’ll wait for the confirmation points above and can lock the kickoff slot.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Tessa — this looks like the right approach and thanks for breaking it down. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Hardware specifics — we want two comparison points: our committed A100 reserved nodes (planned for Q4) and a short H100 pilot you mentioned. Please include the exact instance families you’ll use for each side so we can route procurement questions to cloud ops (we need SKU-level parity to be confident).

2) Quantization baseline — will Redwood run tests with 8-bit and 4-bit quantization variants? We want to see quality-cost tradeoffs explicitly in the matrix.

3) Data residency — for the Dedicated runs, can you confirm where logs/traces will be retained and whether we can restrict retention to 30 days (MedTech compliance ask).

4) Scripts & access — happy for Redwood to run the initial harness, but we want the scripts and the raw results to validate in-house. Please confirm the format of results (CSV + perf traces).

Tentative window Oct 18–29 works, but can we tee up Oct 19 16:00 PT for the pre-run kickoff? That gives us time to confirm procurement SKUs.

Asha — good questions. Quick answers so procurement/cloud ops have what they need: 

- Instance families we’ll use for parity runs:
  * Hyperscaler reserved baseline: c6g.xlarge-equivalent (A100-backed VM) and n2d-h100-equivalent (H100 pilot). We’ll include exact SKUs for AWS/GCP/Azure in the matrix (will list SKU+disk/network profiles).

- Quantization: yes — we will run the following baseline profiles: FP16 (no quant), int8 (8-bit), and 4-bit quant (QLoRA-style/LLM-adapted) where model fidelity remains acceptable. Each profile will include perf + output-sample diffs so you can evaluate quality degradation.

- Data residency/retention: for Dedicated runs logs/traces will be stored in your VPC/Cloud storage if you choose customer-hosted Dedicated. Redwood-hosted Dedicated will store logs in our EU/US region per your selection — retention is configurable; we can set the default to 30 days and provide exportable traces (we’ll note this in the SOW).

- Results format: CSV perf summaries + gzipped perf traces and a JSON summary file. We’ll also provide raw token-level logs on request (redacted) for QA.

Operational ask: please provide the exact procurement contacts and any account IDs we should include for access. If Oct 19 16:00 PT works for MedTech, we’ll schedule and include our infra lead (Rafael) to run through the harness.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
